open_findings.detail: With the incorrect constraint forbidding W2-J4, the solver can assign W2 to J3 (cost 1), leading to a suboptimal objective value of 27.0 compared to the true minimum under correct rules. The solution.json file was not found at the expected path, but the stdout confirms the wrong objective was computed.

The solver produced 27.0 which is lower than the true optimum under correct constraints, indicating it exploited the bug by assigning W2 to J3 (cost 1) while being forced away from J4.

reply.rationale: The finding is an implementation bug: the hard qualification constraint for Business Rule 3 was applied to the wrong job. Line 34 sets x[W2,J4]==0, but the rule requires W2 not be assigned to J3. The fix replaces the forbidden pair (W2,J4) with the correct one (W2,J3). This is a minimal local change; all other logic (assignment constraints, objective, output schema) remains unchanged.
reply.risk_notes: Low risk. Only the single constraint line changes. After the fix, W2 can take J4 (cost 7) and cannot take J3 (cost 1), which may shift the optimal assignment away from using the cheap W2-J3 edge. The solver will recompute the true optimum under the corrected constraint.
